# nish/net/protobuf

Protobuf's wire format, without a schema: a reader that walks the fields of a message held in a `u8[]` span, and a writer that appends fields to a caller's buffer. It knows tags, the four wire types proto3 uses and the value encodings on top of them (varint, zigzag, the little-endian fixed widths, length-delimited spans); what a field number means is the caller's schema, not this module's.

```ts
import {
  PROTO_ERR_DEPTH,
  PROTO_ERR_FIELD,
  PROTO_ERR_GROUP,
  PROTO_ERR_LENGTH,
  PROTO_ERR_MISMATCH,
  PROTO_ERR_TRUNCATED,
  PROTO_ERR_UNBALANCED,
  PROTO_ERR_VARINT,
  PROTO_ERR_WINDOW,
  PROTO_ERR_WIRE_TYPE,
  PROTO_MAX_DEPTH,
  PROTO_MAX_FIELD,
  PROTO_MAX_SIZE,
  PROTO_OK,
  PROTO_WIRE_EGROUP,
  PROTO_WIRE_I32,
  PROTO_WIRE_I64,
  PROTO_WIRE_LEN,
  PROTO_WIRE_SGROUP,
  PROTO_WIRE_VARINT,
  ProtoReader,
  ProtoWriter,
} from "nish/net/protobuf";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { ProtoReader, ProtoWriter, PROTO_OK } from "nish/net/protobuf";

const w = new ProtoWriter([]);
w.uint64(1, toU64(150));
w.string(2, "hi");

const r = new ProtoReader(w.buf, 0, w.end);
while (r.next()) {
  if (r.field === 1) {
    const id: u64 = r.uint64();
  } else if (r.field === 2) {
    const n: i32 = r.len(); // the bytes are w.buf[r.spanStart, r.spanStart + n)
  }                         // any other field is skipped by the next call to next()
}
if (r.failed !== PROTO_OK) {
  // a negative PROTO_ERR_* code: the message is malformed
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="Proto​Reader" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#protoreader">

Reads the fields of one protobuf message from `buf[from, to)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Proto​Writer" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#protowriter">

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**The reader refuses with a code, never a panic.** Peer bytes cannot make
it read outside its span: every value is checked against the span's end
before a byte of it is read. The first fault sets `failed` to a negative
`PROTO_ERR_*` code, which is sticky: every later call answers `false` or
zero until `reset`. It refuses a varint whose tenth byte still has its
continuation bit, a varint or fixed value that runs off the span, a length
past the span, a tag whose field number is 0 or whose varint is above
2^32 - 1 (so a field number past 2^29 - 1), the group wire types 3 and 4,
the undefined wire types 6 and 7, an `enter` past `PROTO_MAX_DEPTH`
nested spans, and a typed read whose wire type is not the field's.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="A field the caller does not read is skipped by its wire type">

**A field the caller does not read is skipped by its wire type** when
`next` is called again, so an unknown field is checked and passed, never
interpreted. A varint's bits past the 64th (the tenth byte's top six) are
dropped, and an over-long varint (`0x80 0x00` for 0) is read as
its value; neither can move the reader outside its span.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The writer appends to the caller's buffer">

**The writer appends to the caller's buffer** from `end`, storing over the
bytes already there and pushing past its length, so a buffer that has grown
to a message's size is reused without allocating once the writer is `reset`.
Misuse (a field number outside 1 to 2^29 - 1, nesting past
`PROTO_MAX_DEPTH`, an `endMessage` or a packed element with no open
message, a `bytes` window outside its source array, a message past
`PROTO_MAX_SIZE` bytes) sets the same sticky `failed` code and writes nothing more. Neither side panics: a
reader window outside its array is `PROTO_ERR_WINDOW` too, so a program
held to no panic may call both.

</scalar-detail>

The record of what this module refuses and why is
`docs/security/protobuf.md`.

## Classes

### ProtoReader

Reads the fields of one protobuf message from `buf[from, to)`. `next`
moves to the next field and answers its number and wire type in `field`
and `wireType`; one typed read then takes its value, or the next call to
`next` skips it. `enter` and `leave` walk an embedded message, and
`enterPacked` and `more` the elements of a packed repeated field.

```ts
class ProtoReader
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ProtoReader(buf: readonly u8[], from: i32, to: i32)` | A reader over `buf[from, to)`. |
| `buf: readonly u8[]` | The array the message is in; the reader never writes to it. |
| `depth: i32` | How many spans are entered. |
| `end: i32` | The end of the span being read: the message's, or the entered field's. |
| `failed: i32` | `PROTO_OK`, or the first `PROTO_ERR_*` code; sticky until `reset`. |
| `field: i32` | The current field's number, 1 to 2^29 - 1, after `next` answers `true`. |
| `pos: i32` | The offset of the next byte to read. |
| `spanStart: i32` | Where the bytes of the last value `len` read begin in `buf`. |
| `wireType: i32` | The current field's wire type, one of the `PROTO_WIRE_*` values. |
| `bool(): boolean` | Reads the current varint field as a bool: any value but 0 is `true`. |
| `double(): f64` | Reads the current 64-bit field as a double. |
| `enter(): boolean` | Enters the current length-delimited field as an embedded message: `next` then reads its fields, until `leave`. |
| `enterPacked(wireType: i32): boolean` | Enters the current length-delimited field as a packed repeated field whose elements have `wireType`: `more` then moves from element to element, until `leave`. |
| `fixed32(): u32` | Reads the current 32-bit field as a fixed32. |
| `fixed64(): u64` | Reads the current 64-bit field as a fixed64. |
| `float(): f32` | Reads the current 32-bit field as a float. A signaling NaN comes back quiet, its top mantissa bit set; `fixed32` reads the exact bits. |
| `int32(): i32` | Reads the current varint field as an int32, keeping its low 32 bits: a negative int32 arrives sign-extended to ten bytes. |
| `int64(): i64` | Reads the current varint field as an int64. |
| `leave(): boolean` | Leaves the span `enter` or `enterPacked` opened, skipping what is left of it the way `next` or `more` would, so a malformed rest is refused, and returns to the enclosing span. |
| `len(): i32` | Reads the current length-delimited field as a span of bytes: a string, bytes, or a message to read later with a reader of its own. The span begins at `spanStart` in `buf`; a string's bytes are not checked to be UTF-8, which is the caller's to decode. |
| `more(): boolean` | Moves to the next element of the entered packed field, skipping the current one if it was not read. A typed read then takes it. |
| `next(): boolean` | Moves to the next field of the span, skipping the current field's value if it was not read. |
| `reset(buf: readonly u8[], from: i32, to: i32): void` | Starts over on `buf[from, to)`, clearing `failed`. A window outside `buf` is a caller bug: the reader holds an empty span and `failed` is `PROTO_ERR_WINDOW`. |
| `sfixed32(): i32` | Reads the current 32-bit field as an sfixed32. |
| `sfixed64(): i64` | Reads the current 64-bit field as an sfixed64. |
| `sint32(): i32` | Reads the current varint field as a zigzag-coded sint32, from its low 32 bits. |
| `sint64(): i64` | Reads the current varint field as a zigzag-coded sint64. |
| `uint32(): u32` | Reads the current varint field as a uint32, keeping its low 32 bits as protobuf does. |
| `uint64(): u64` | Reads the current varint field as a uint64. |

### ProtoWriter

Writes protobuf fields into `buf` from offset 0, up to `end`. An embedded
message or packed field is written between `beginMessage` and
`endMessage`, which fills in its length.

```ts
class ProtoWriter
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ProtoWriter(buf: u8[])` | A writer into `buf`, which it grows as the message needs and reuses after `reset`. |
| `buf: u8[]` | The caller's buffer: the message is `buf[0, end)`; bytes past `end` are stale. |
| `depth: i32` | How many messages are open. |
| `end: i32` | The offset one past the last byte written. |
| `failed: i32` | `PROTO_OK`, or the first `PROTO_ERR_*` code; sticky until `reset`. |
| `beginMessage(field: i32): void` | Opens a length-delimited field, an embedded message or a packed repeated field, whose contents are the fields or elements written until `endMessage`. |
| `bool(field: i32, v: boolean): void` | Writes a bool field. |
| `bytes(field: i32, src: readonly u8[], from: i32, count: i32): void` | Writes a bytes field from `src[from, from + count)`. A window outside `src` is a caller bug: nothing is written and `failed` is `PROTO_ERR_WINDOW`. |
| `double(field: i32, v: f64): void` | Writes a double field. |
| `endMessage(): void` | Closes the field `beginMessage` opened, writing its length; contents of 128 bytes or more are moved right to make room for a longer length. |
| `fixed32(field: i32, v: u32): void` | Writes a fixed32 field. |
| `fixed64(field: i32, v: u64): void` | Writes a fixed64 field. |
| `float(field: i32, v: f32): void` | Writes a float field. |
| `int32(field: i32, v: i32): void` | Writes an int32 field, a negative value sign-extended to ten bytes as protobuf requires. |
| `int64(field: i32, v: i64): void` | Writes an int64 field; a negative value takes ten bytes. |
| `packedFixed32(v: u32): void` | Writes one element of the packed field the last `beginMessage` opened, as four little-endian bytes: a fixed32, an sfixed32 or a float's bits. Open spans are checked as `packedVarint` checks them. |
| `packedFixed64(v: u64): void` | Writes one element of the packed field the last `beginMessage` opened, as eight little-endian bytes: a fixed64, an sfixed64 or a double's bits. Open spans are checked as `packedVarint` checks them. |
| `packedVarint(v: u64): void` | Writes one element of the packed field the last `beginMessage` opened, as a varint: a uint64, or an int64, int32 or bool converted to `u64` as `int64`, `int32` and `bool` do. With no span open it sets `PROTO_ERR_UNBALANCED`; that the open span is a packed field, not an embedded message, is the caller's to guarantee. |
| `reset(): void` | Starts a new message at offset 0 of the same buffer, clearing `failed`. |
| `sfixed32(field: i32, v: i32): void` | Writes an sfixed32 field. |
| `sfixed64(field: i32, v: i64): void` | Writes an sfixed64 field. |
| `sint32(field: i32, v: i32): void` | Writes a zigzag-coded sint32 field. |
| `sint64(field: i32, v: i64): void` | Writes a zigzag-coded sint64 field. |
| `string(field: i32, s: string): void` | Writes a string field: the string's UTF-8 bytes. |
| `uint32(field: i32, v: u32): void` | Writes a uint32 field. |
| `uint64(field: i32, v: u64): void` | Writes a uint64 field. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="100" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_MAX_DEPTH: i32`

How many spans `ProtoReader.enter` and `ProtoWriter.beginMessage` may nest, protobuf's own default recursion limit.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="536,870,911" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_MAX_FIELD: i32`

The largest field number, 2^29 - 1.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2,147,483,646" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_MAX_SIZE: i32`

The largest message the writer writes, 2^31 - 2 bytes, so that its `end` fits an `i32`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="-7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_DEPTH: i32`

More than `PROTO_MAX_DEPTH` nested spans.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_FIELD: i32`

A field number of 0 or past 2^29 - 1: read in a tag, or given to a writer.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_GROUP: i32`

A tag with the group wire types 3 or 4, which proto3 does not have.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_LENGTH: i32`

A length-delimited value's length is past the end of the span.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_MISMATCH: i32`

A read whose wire type is not the current field's, or of a value already read.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_TRUNCATED: i32`

A varint or a fixed-width value runs past the end of the span.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_UNBALANCED: i32`

A `leave` or `endMessage` with no span open, or a packed element written outside one.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_VARINT: i32`

A varint's tenth byte has its continuation bit set: no varint is longer than ten bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_WINDOW: i32`

A reader window or a `bytes` source window outside its array, or a message that would grow past `PROTO_MAX_SIZE` bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_ERR_WIRE_TYPE: i32`

A tag with the wire types 6 or 7, which protobuf does not define.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PROTO_OK: i32`

No fault.

</scalar-card>
